events.extended_summary: President Donald Trump adopted a stronger tone toward Russia, telling Vladimir Putin to halt military aggression against Europe and pull back to secure a peace deal with Ukraine. In comments posted Thursday, Trump said he urged the Russian leader during conversations in China last week to end military aggression across the continent to facilitate a rapid agreement between Russia and Ukraine. He also warned Putin not to widen the war against Ukraine. The remarks followed a Wednesday evening meeting with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte at Mar-a-Lago in Florida, where the pair issued a joint statement calling on Putin not to expand the conflict and to resolve it peacefully as rapidly as possible. They also discussed boosting defense spending in both the United States and NATO. The Kremlin responded by accusing Kyiv of attempting to spread the war to the Mediterranean and Baltic seas, referencing Ukraine's sinking of a Russian naval corvette in a Libyan port on Sunday.
events.micro_summary: President Trump urged Putin to halt military aggression against Europe and secure a peace deal with Ukraine.
events.summary: President Trump told Vladimir Putin to halt military aggression against Europe and pull back to secure a peace deal with Ukraine, warning against widening the war after meeting NATO chief Mark Rutte at Mar-a-Lago.

events.extended_summary: Volodymyr Zelensky voiced frustration with the United States in an interview, saying delays in delivering anti-ballistic missiles are costing Ukrainian lives and that Washington is not pushing Russia hard enough during peace negotiations. He described as "strange" Donald Trump's social media post showing him embracing Vladimir Putin as "my friend," stating that Putin is an aggressor and killer who cannot be a friend, comparing the situation to befriending Adolf Hitler during World War II. Zelensky noted that the latest round of peace talks mediated in Abu Dhabi earlier this month made no obvious progress, with talks expected to resume in December. While Trump posted that he urged Russia to pull back military aggression, Russia appears to have returned to hardline negotiating positions. Meanwhile, Russian strikes have grown more frequent and deadly, with civilian casualties reaching an all-time high during five years of full-scale invasion.
events.micro_summary: Zelensky calls Trump's friendship with Putin 'strange' and says the Russian leader is a killer.
events.summary: Volodymyr Zelensky criticized Donald Trump's friendship with Vladimir Putin as 'strange,' calling the Russian leader an aggressor and killer, while urging the US to push harder for peace talks amid stalled negotiations and rising civilian deaths.

events.extended_summary: Spain holds snap general elections on 29 November, called eight months early by Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez after MPs rejected planned housing law changes and nationwide protests followed the eviction and subsequent death of 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal in Madrid. Polls open at 09:00 and close at 20:00, with provisional results expected an hour later. Opinion polls place Alberto Núñez Feijóo's conservative People's Party narrowly ahead of Sánchez's Socialist PSOE, with the far-right Vox party third. While the PP is projected to fall short of an outright majority, together with Vox it is expected to hold enough seats to govern, mirroring the coalition already ruling Andalusia since May. Key voter concerns include housing costs, which have risen over 80% since 2015, high cost of living, corruption, immigration, and a recent devastating rail disaster. Nearly 39 million of Spain's almost 50 million population are eligible to vote.
events.micro_summary: Spain votes in snap elections on 29 November with the People's Party narrowly leading polls against Prime Minister Sánchez's Socialists.
events.summary: Spain votes in snap elections on 29 November after Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called the poll early following housing protests. Polls show Alberto Núñez Feijóo's People's Party narrowly ahead of Sánchez's Socialists with Vox third, requiring Vox support to govern.

events.extended_summary: Russia has started deploying its Rassvet satellite constellation, developed by Bureau 1440, for military communications and attacks over Ukraine. The system, which operates in low Earth orbit, is being used to improve strike accuracy, expand reconnaissance drone capabilities, and strengthen resilience against electronic warfare. First launches of serial Rassvet satellites occurred in March and July 2026. This deployment follows Russia's loss of access to SpaceX's Starlink network in early 2026, when SpaceX and the Ukrainian Defense Ministry implemented a whitelist that deactivated terminals used by Russian forces. Prior to this cutoff, Russian military units had acquired Starlink terminals through third countries to maintain communications in the battle zone. Since losing Starlink access, the Ukrainian army has recaptured approximately 400 square kilometers of territory. Ukrainian military intelligence reports that while Rassvet is now operational, the constellation remains insufficient to provide uninterrupted coverage of Ukrainian territory.
events.micro_summary: Russia deploys Rassvet satellite network for military operations in Ukraine after losing Starlink access.
events.summary: Russia has begun using its Rassvet satellite system for military communications and attacks over Ukraine, aiming to improve strike accuracy and drone capabilities after losing access to Starlink terminals in early 2026.

events.extended_summary: NATO chief Mark Rutte stated the alliance will defend against threats in space after claims indicated Russia is preparing to launch a nuclear-armed satellite within 60 days. The satellite, named Sputnik-S, carries a nuclear warhead capable of disrupting or destroying other satellites. Rutte vowed NATO would defend every inch of its territory, including space, and would assess deterrence options. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz called the claims shocking, revealing Russia's escalation. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov dismissed the stories, while the Russian embassy rejected the allegations as unfounded propaganda. Russia is a signatory to the 1967 Outer Space Treaty banning weapons of mass destruction from orbit. European Space Agency head Josef Aschbacher called nuclear weapons in space the ultimate nightmare scenario, while Durham University's Bleddyn Bowen warned of massive infrastructural effects from a space nuclear explosion.
events.micro_summary: NATO and Germany respond to claims that Russia plans to launch a nuclear-armed satellite within 60 days.
events.summary: NATO chief Mark Rutte and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz addressed claims that Russia plans to launch a nuclear-armed satellite dubbed Sputnik-S within 60 days, with Rutte vowing NATO will defend space and Merz calling the claims shocking.

events.extended_summary: The Nations Championship finals week at Twickenham requires unprecedented logistical coordination to host more than 550 players and support staff from the world's top 12 teams for six matches compressed into three days at a single venue. Organizers made block bookings at hotels across Brentford, Guildford, Cobham and beyond to accommodate teams during a busy Black Friday shopping weekend, with chefs and nutritionists ensuring adequate supplies for high-energy diets. Each team received private training facilities at local clubs, schools and universities, with choices based on world rankings, while South Africa secured the Teddington base. Teams conduct eve-of-match captain's runs at training grounds rather than the venue. Special requests included Argentina's asado barbecue and Japan's imported rice cooker. Each team was provided four vehicles including a bus, people carrier, kit van and equipment truck to transport players between accommodations, training bases and Twickenham.
events.micro_summary: Organizers coordinate unprecedented logistics for Nations Championship finals week hosting 550 players from 12 teams at Twickenham.
events.summary: The Nations Championship finals week brings over 550 players and staff from 12 teams to Twickenham for six matches in three days, requiring block-booked hotels, private training grounds, and specialized catering including Argentina's asado and Japan's rice cooker.

events.extended_summary: Police located stolen trophies at a home on Orrong Road in Elsternwick around 10am Thursday, but three Melbourne Cup trophies won by Makybe Diva between 2003 and 2005 and the 1948 Caulfield Cup remain missing. The Melbourne Cups are valued at $3 million. A 39-year-old man arrested on November 16 over a Caulfield Racecourse theft was charged with burglary and theft, then re-arrested and charged with offences relating to a Flemington Racecourse heist where the Makybe Diva trophies were stolen from a smashed cabinet around 6.30am on November 16. He was bailed to appear at Moorabbin Magistrates' Court on March 1. A 36-year-old man was also charged with burglary, theft and dealing proceeds of crime. The 1948 Caulfield Cup was allegedly stolen between November 4 and 11, while a fourth Melbourne Cup was taken on November 12. Makybe Diva's former owner Tony Santic was devastated by the theft.
events.micro_summary: Stolen racing trophies found at Melbourne home while three Melbourne Cups worth $3 million remain missing.

events.extended_summary: The Buffalo Bills (9-1) host the Kansas City Chiefs (8-2) in the final primetime game of the NFL's Thanksgiving Day slate. Buffalo, tied for the best record in the league, can become the first 10-win team with a victory over Kansas City. The Chiefs have previously spoiled Bills' success, as Patrick Mahomes has defeated Josh Allen and Buffalo four times in the postseason. Kansas City enters the matchup following a 34-7 victory over the Arizona Cardinals, with Mahomes throwing for 672 yards and eight touchdowns over his last two games. Weather in Buffalo is expected to be poor, with temperatures around 37 degrees, a high chance of rain, and 19 mile-per-hour winds. Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III is missing the game with a groin issue.
events.micro_summary: Buffalo Bills host Kansas City Chiefs in Thanksgiving Day finale with 9-1 and 8-2 records.
events.summary: The Buffalo Bills (9-1) host the Kansas City Chiefs (8-2) in the final Thanksgiving Day NFL game, with Buffalo seeking to become the first 10-win team and Kansas City looking to spoil their rival's milestone.

events.extended_summary: The Philadelphia Eagles defeated the Dallas Cowboys 39-38 in a Thanksgiving Day game in Dallas after erasing a 31-10 deficit. Eagles kicker Jake Elliott won the game with a 59-yard field goal with two seconds remaining. Eagles quarterback Joe Milton threw for 331 yards with three touchdown passes and scored a rushing touchdown in his best career performance. Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott threw for 291 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions, while CeeDee Lamb had 134 receiving yards and Javonte Williams scored three total touchdowns. Eagles receiver DeVonta Smith caught 11 passes for 200 yards and two touchdowns. The Eagles also blocked a punt for a touchdown, while Cowboys kicker Brandon Aubrey missed a 40-yard field goal in the fourth quarter. The loss dropped Dallas to 5-7, while Philadelphia improved to 4-7.
events.micro_summary: The Eagles defeated the Cowboys 39-38 on Thanksgiving with a 59-yard field goal as time expired.
events.summary: The Eagles defeated the Cowboys 39-38 in Dallas on Thanksgiving after overcoming a 31-10 deficit, with Jake Elliott hitting a 59-yard field goal with two seconds left.

events.extended_summary: Severe storms battered the US East Coast on Thanksgiving, prompting states of emergency in New York and New Jersey as winds up to 70mph knocked out power to approximately 800,000 homes and businesses. Macy's postponed its 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade through Manhattan for the first time in history, rescheduling it for Saturday morning due to safety concerns about high winds. More than 400 flights were cancelled and at least 1,700 delayed nationwide, while coastal flooding between North Carolina and New Jersey closed roads and forced emergency rescues. Gusts of 50-70mph were recorded across Virginia, Maryland, Delaware, New Jersey, New York and New England, ripping the roof off an apartment building in Ocean City, Maryland, and crushing houses with falling trees. Tornado warnings sounded in Norfolk, Virginia, and nearly two million people in Maryland counties were asked to conserve water due to power disruptions.
events.micro_summary: Thanksgiving storms leave 800,000 without power and force first-ever postponement of Macy's parade.
events.summary: Severe storms battered the US East Coast on Thanksgiving, leaving 800,000 without power, cancelling hundreds of flights, and forcing Macy's to postpone its 100th parade for the first time as New York and New Jersey declared states of emergency.

events.extended_summary: Ukraine carried out attacks against Russian vessels in Libyan waters off Benghazi port, claiming it sank a Russian warship and struck a cargo vessel transporting military equipment. The strike killed two naval officers of the self-styled Libyan National Army. Italy denounced the operation as a violation of Libya's sovereignty, with Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani stating Rome had received no prior notice of the strike in Libyan territorial waters. Libya's eastern-based forces, led by the LNA, condemned the attack as a declaration of war and promised retaliation. The Tripoli-based Presidential Council also called the strike a declaration of war against the Libyan state and held Ukraine fully responsible. Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha described the vessels as legitimate targets, asserting Kyiv's right to self-defense against Russian aggression while stating the actions were not intended to harm Libya. The United Nations mission in Libya called for an independent investigation into the incident.
events.micro_summary: Ukraine sank a Russian warship in Libyan waters, killing two officers and drawing Italy's condemnation.
events.summary: Ukraine attacked Russian vessels in Libyan waters near Benghazi, sinking a warship and killing two Libyan National Army officers. Italy denounced the strike as a violation of Libya's sovereignty, while Libyan authorities condemned it as a declaration of war.

events.extended_summary: A massive fire erupted at multiple buildings in Lavallette, New Jersey on Thanksgiving afternoon, destroying one vacant home and damaging another. The blaze, which occurred around 3 p.m. on Jersey City Avenue less than a block from the ocean, escalated to four alarms. High winds from a storm in the area were present, though officials have not determined whether weather conditions caused the fire. Emergency services responded to the scene and continued working to control the flames. The vacant home collapsed due to the fire, while flames spread to a neighboring residence causing damage. No injuries have been reported. The cause of the fire remains under investigation and has not yet been announced.
events.micro_summary: A four-alarm fire destroyed a vacant home and damaged another in Lavallette on Thanksgiving.
events.summary: A massive fire destroyed one vacant home and damaged another in Lavallette, New Jersey on Thanksgiving afternoon. The blaze reached four alarms amid high winds, but no injuries were reported and the cause remains undetermined.

events.extended_summary: Ramayana: Rise of a Legend has accumulated Rs 1,777 crore in worldwide gross collections over 22 days, comprising Rs 1,185 crore domestically and Rs 592 crore from overseas markets. The film earned Rs 9.65 crore net in India and Rs 10 crore internationally on its fourth Friday, bringing its total India net collection to Rs 992.10 crore, just Rs 7.90 crore short of the Rs 1,000 crore domestic net milestone. Its first week generated Rs 564 crore net, followed by Rs 299 crore in the second week and Rs 128.35 crore in the third. Daily collections have slowed, with the film earning Rs 9.50 crore on day 21 after a boost to Rs 17.50 crore on day 20 from discounted tickets. The Hindi version contributed Rs 6.75 crore from 13,287 shows on Thursday, while show counts have declined from over 25,000 to approximately 15,418.
events.micro_summary: Ramayana: Rise of a Legend reaches Rs 1,777 crore worldwide gross in 22 days.
events.summary: Ramayana: Rise of a Legend collected Rs 1,777 crore worldwide in 22 days, with Rs 992.10 crore net domestically, nearing the Rs 1,000 crore milestone after earning Rs 9.65 crore on its fourth Friday.

events.extended_summary: Actor-filmmaker Arjun Sarja has joined producer Anoop Mohan for an ambitious patriotic pan-India film under Presidential Movies International Private Limited, marking the production house's third feature. Sarja will serve as both director and lead actor. The announcement was made on November 25 via an Instagram post. The film's muhurtham ceremony is scheduled for November 27, 2026, at the Sri Ram Janmabhoomi Temple in Ayodhya, where the official title will be unveiled. The story and screenplay have been written by retired Army officer Major Vijay Bhargavan, with Thomas Roy serving as executive producer. The project aims to combine emotional resonance with cinematic grandeur while exploring themes of courage, sacrifice, duty, and patriotism. Sarja was last seen in the Tamil film Blast and is next set to appear in Polimera 3.
events.micro_summary: Arjun Sarja will direct and star in a pan-India patriotic film produced by Anoop Mohan, muhurtham November 27, 2026.
events.summary: Arjun Sarja will direct and star in a patriotic pan-India film produced by Anoop Mohan. The muhurtham is set for November 27, 2026, at Sri Ram Janmabhoomi Temple in Ayodhya, where the title will be unveiled.

events.extended_summary: Nitesh Tiwari's "Ramayana" has doubled visitor numbers at Kerala's Jatayu Earth's Center, known locally as Jatayu Rock, Ministry of Tourism joint secretary Harikishore S. said at a WAVES Film Bazaar panel in Goa. The site is traditionally held to be where the mythical bird Jatayu fell after battling Ravana. Indian officials used the session, "Filming in India: India's Rise as a Global Production Hub," to pitch a single-window filming portal and state incentives to international producers. The India Cine Hub portal, first launched November 21, 2015, now combines permission applications with directories of crew, equipment, services, an interactive location map, and incentive information. State governments, local administrations, and central agencies including Railways, the Archaeological Survey of India, and civil aviation authorities sit behind the single window, with each state having a nodal officer. The Ministry of Tourism has also signed a non-binding MoU with Netflix, Amazon, and JioCinema to encourage content about India and shooting in the country.
events.micro_summary: Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana doubled visitors at Kerala's Jatayu Earth's Center, officials said at WAVES Film Bazaar.
events.summary: Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana doubled visitors at Kerala's Jatayu Earth's Center, a Ministry of Tourism official said at the WAVES Film Bazaar in Goa, where India promoted its single-window filming portal and state incentives to international producers.

events.extended_summary: India captain Shubman Gill won the toss and elected to bowl first against New Zealand in the second Test at Hagley Oval in Christchurch. India made one change to their playing XI, handing a Test debut to 26-year-old pacer Gurnoor Brar, who replaced Prasidh Krishna after the first Test in Wellington ended in a draw. New Zealand decided to go with the same playing XI for the series-deciding match. Former India captain Sunil Gavaskar questioned the omission of Ravindra Jadeja, noting he is India's third-highest wicket-taker in the ongoing World Test Championship cycle and that his spin would have been useful on the fourth and fifth days. Gavaskar also mentioned Mohammed Siraj's absence but ultimately backed the team selection, stating that once the playing XI is announced, everyone should support the team.
events.micro_summary: India elected to bowl first in the second Test against New Zealand in Christchurch after winning the toss.
events.summary: India captain Shubman Gill won the toss and elected to bowl first against New Zealand in the second Test at Hagley Oval in Christchurch, handing a Test debut to pacer Gurnoor Brar while leaving out Ravindra Jadeja and Mohammed Siraj.

events.extended_summary: India fast bowler Mohammed Shami has stated he is not considering the 2027 ODI World Cup or 2028 T20 World Cup, focusing instead on maintaining his rhythm through domestic cricket and the IPL. The 36-year-old, who took 24 wickets as leading wicket-taker at the 2023 World Cup and nine wickets at the 2025 Champions Trophy, retired from Test cricket earlier this month. He plans to play in the Vijay Hazare Trophy next month to demonstrate his capabilities and maintain fitness. Shami emphasized that his motivation comes from enjoying the game and sharing experience with younger players, stating he will continue playing white-ball cricket and red-ball cricket if required. He dismissed suggestions that his domestic participation relates to retirement, leaving future selection decisions to the selectors.
events.micro_summary: Mohammed Shami focuses on domestic cricket and IPL, dismissing thoughts of 2027 and 2028 World Cups.
events.summary: India fast bowler Mohammed Shami says he is focused on domestic cricket and the IPL, leaving selection decisions to selectors while dismissing thoughts of the 2027 ODI World Cup and 2028 T20 World Cup.

events.extended_summary: Sri Lanka A defeated India A by 8 wickets in the first semi-final of the Asia Cup Rising Stars tournament in Doha. Chasing a target of 318 runs, Sri Lanka A scored 318 runs with the loss of 2 wickets in 41.3 overs. India A batted first and scored 317 runs losing 8 wickets in 50 overs. Abhishek Sharma scored 78 runs off 63 balls for India A. Sineth scored 105 off 70 balls for Sri Lanka A and Jayawardena was declared player of the match. Sri Lanka A will play the final on Sunday against the winner of the second semi-final between Pakistan A and Bangladesh A.
events.micro_summary: Sri Lanka A defeated India A by 8 wickets chasing 318 runs to reach the Asia Cup Rising Stars final.
events.summary: Sri Lanka A defeated India A by 8 wickets in the Asia Cup Rising Stars semi-final in Doha, chasing 318 runs to score 318/2 in 41.3 overs after India A posted 317/8.

events.extended_summary: Christchurch (New Zealand) (AFP) – New Zealand were 77-1 at lunch Friday on the first day of the second Test against India, after being asked to bat on a green wicket. Captain Tom Latham was 42 and Devon Conway was out for 31 with the last ball before lunch, lbw to Gurnoor Brar. Indian captain Shubman Gill won the toss - India's 10th toss win in 12 matches during the tour - and elected to field. The Hagley Oval pitch had long and dense grass coverage, leading both captains to expect pace and bounce throughout the Test. India made one change to their starting side from the drawn first Test in Wellington, offering a debut to speedster Brar in place of Prasidh Krishna. New Zealand named an unchanged team.
